answer: A stake-weighted reputation market resists fake identities by making each one costly: an agent must lock real funds behind its name, and peers rate its work over time, so a newcomer starts with no trust and must earn it. Like a velvet rope at a club, the deposit filters throwaway accounts; an attacker who spawns an island of fake identities must fund every one, and slashing burns the stake of any that misbehave. Shale-thin trust built on nothing crumbles, but stake-backed history is expensive to counterfeit at scale.
